## Do Google refresh tokens expire? The 6 conditions
| # | Condition | When it fires | Severity | Fix |
|-|-|-|-|-|
| 1 | **App in testing mode - 7-day limit** | OAuth consent screen is "Testing" and app is not verified by Google | Critical | Publish the app or use an internal Workspace app |

## The 7-day testing trap: why it happens, how to escape
To protect users, Google automatically expires all refresh tokens issued by unverified apps after exactly **7 days**. The cap also applies to [the 100 test user limit](https://www.unipile.com/google-oauth-100-user-limit/) for apps in testing mode.

Once published, **google oauth refresh token lifetime becomes indefinite** (subject to the remaining 5 conditions).

Internal apps are not subject to the 7-day expiration or the 100 test user cap.

## Google OAuth Refresh Token - FAQ
The most common is the **7-day testing limit**: if your app is in "Testing" status in Google Cloud Console, all refresh tokens expire after 7 days.

In **testing mode**: 7 days maximum, regardless of use.

The **google oauth refresh token 7-day expiration** applies when your OAuth consent screen status is "Testing" in Google Cloud Console. Google enforces this limit on all unverified applications as a security measure. It also coincides with the [100 test user limit](https://www.unipile.com/google-oauth-100-user-limit/).
